source_refs.note: Topic 14.4.6 with the Interesting Information box, printed page 309.

blocks.text: The decrease in the concentration of ozone in the stratosphere is called depletion of ozone, caused by organic compounds called chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), which are gases or low-boiling liquids at room temperature used as aerosol propellants and refrigerants. CFCs diffuse into the stratosphere, where ultraviolet radiation breaks them down to give chlorine free radicals, which break down ozone: CFCl3 with UV gives CFCl2 + Cl.; Cl. + O3 gives ClO. + O2; ClO. + O2 gives Cl. + O2. The chlorine radical formed in the last step can attack another ozone molecule, so the second and third steps repeat many times: the decomposition of one CFC molecule can destroy up to 100,000 molecules of ozone. CFCs are also 100,000 times more effective than CO2 at trapping heat in the atmosphere.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book's third step, ClO. + O2 giving Cl. + O2, is not balanced. The step in the ozone-destroying cycle is ClO. + O giving Cl. + O2: an oxygen atom takes the oxygen from ClO. and the chlorine radical is set free again.
